title: A 14-token exact orbit exposes selection bias from freezing a tied stopword
statement: In a uniform block containing A five times, B five times and C four times, the frozen first-occurring top type gives 15,042 rejections among 252,252 orders at nominal .05 in the compress statistic. Reselecting the first top type inside the exact permutation gives zero rejections at .05. In 48 piecewise independent synthetic books, reselecting gives 48/48 rejections in both modes when whole blocks are permuted, versus 1/48 compress and 2/48 barrier with the independently known sub-block boundaries.
check: Use a tie-invariant statistic when supported or recompute any order-dependent selection within each null draw. Freeze an independent block rationale and test it on weaker noisy ciphers, nearby alternative boundaries and held-back historical sources. Measure specificity separately against reversible local dependence and within-block relationships.
protocol:
# P-J-044 expanded public calibration

Preserve the published ratio of distinct unordered pairs with absolute directional count difference >5, using distances 1–3. Preserve physical scoring blocks in every statistic. With compression, remove the selected top type(s) before forming pairs. With barriers, a dropped token blocks every pair spanning it. Count complete first/last and interior eligibility identically in observed and null books.

Compare a single top stopword chosen by earliest occurrence among frequency ties in each observed book and then fixed in null draws, the same rule recomputed in every null draw, and all tied top types retained together as the removal set. The frequency definition uses the whole book. Use 99 within-exchangeability-block shuffles with add-one upper-tail p≤.05 and the same permuted words across methods. Compare integer count ratios by cross multiplication. A choice that leaves no eligible pair is unsupported, including a reference with no eligible pair. Summarize p differences, support and Wilson 95% intervals for independent synthetic books. Check fixed-seed bijective relabeling.

Synthetic books have 24 scoring blocks of 48 positions. For each setting generate 48 independently seeded books. Study exchangeable single-top, exchangeable two-top tie, exchangeable all-tied, block-specific inventory ties, piecewise-independent positional inventories, stationary reversible local persistence, and noisy planted directional cycles at 2% and 8% replacement with an invertible word relabeling. Include these auxiliary checks: common whole-block shuffling, then four aligned 12-position strata and phase-shifted 12-position strata within each block for the piecewise generator. The aligned boundaries come from the generator, independently of the observations. Persistence is a known directional-symmetry control, not a within-block exchangeable null; describe its rejection rate separately. Noise can break a tie, so report realized ties. The planted cycle result concerns those effects and that cipher only.

For external checks use six predeclared independent authors, with 24 equal-length token blocks per source, ignoring printed line ends. Treat naturally ordered book data as descriptive. Use four independent conditional randomizations of the same exact block inventories per work for known-negative calibration and repeated reference, report them by source without treating the 24 samples as independent historical books. No Voynich manuscript or hidden pages enter the study.

Auxiliary historical derivatives equalize the two highest counts by deterministic aliasing of excess instances of the unique top type. This deliberately modified companion is paired with its source and is neither a new independent author nor a proxy for its natural word order.

findings: In the exact 14-token case the compressed numerator is extreme for six of the 126 retained B/C orders. Freezing the stopword gives p=6/126 for every extreme observed order. Across the complete original orbit, 15,042 outcomes are extreme under the first-occurring tied stop selection. Correct recomputation therefore gives p=15,042/252,252 for those outcomes. The all-ties strategy leaves only C and no measurable pairs.

The A6/B6/C5 compression control gives 307,820 exact extreme orders out of 5,717,712, compared with a frozen extreme p of 247,520/5,717,712. The 14-token barrier rule is conservative at .05 but shows inflation at its own smaller p-grid point: 8,360 actual tail outcomes versus 7,896 reported frozen.

The smaller exact orbits are illustrative. The 14-token case was deliberately constructed as a counterexample and independently checked by counting the insertions of the removed type; it does not estimate prevalence in manuscripts.

Across the four synthetic whole-block exchangeable settings, reselected and fixed changes in p were frequent when there are ties. Decisions differed for two tiered-inventory compress trials and exchanged one rejection in each direction. The nominal rate failure in the exact example would be hard to identify with only 48 trials.

Aligned sub-block shuffling preserves the independent positional inventories in the piecewise generator. Shifting the sub-blocks by six words gives 46/48 compress and 37/48 barrier rejections for the reselected rule.

Every rule and both policies reject 48/48 strong enciphered-cycle books at either replacement probability. They also reject 48/48 reversible persistence controls that break the exchangeability assumptions. These are exploratory sensitivity checks on the stated generators.

All six natural historical samples have a single most frequent type. Four exceed the shuffled reference at the .05 cutoff in both modes, and none of the 24 conditional permutations of their block inventories reject. The six capped derivatives have two maximally frequent types by construction. Their conditional negatives reuse each source's material and are not independent documents.
A separate scalar reference reproduced 432 integer pair counts, preserving all stratum multisets. Eight scenarios also verify bijective relabeling invariance using the same shuffle stream.

prepare-historical.py.text:
from collections import Counter
from hashlib import sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys


WIDTH = 48
NUMBER_OF_BLOCKS = 24
SPAN = WIDTH * NUMBER_OF_BLOCKS
METHOD_TAG = "P-J-044-top-frequency-cap-v1"
NATURAL_SCOPE = "First 1152 normalized archived word tokens in source order, contiguous 48-word artificial blocks."


def digest(data):
    return sha256(data).hexdigest()


def selected_blocks(words):
    assert len(words) == SPAN
    return [words[i:i + WIDTH] for i in range(0, SPAN, WIDTH)]


def source_manifest(archive, item_id, record):
    data = (archive / record["file"]).read_bytes()
    assert digest(data) == record["sha256"], item_id
    words = data.decode("utf-8").split()[:SPAN]
    leading = Counter(words).most_common()
    assert len(leading) >= 2, item_id
    count = leading[0][1]
    return {
        "id": item_id,
        "author": record["author"],
        "title": record["title"],
        "language": record["language"],
        "url": record["source_url"],
        "catalog_url": record["catalog_url"],
        "source_sha256": record["sha256"],
        "raw_archived_sha256": record["raw_sha256"],
        "selected_token_stream_sha256": digest(("\n".join(words) + "\n").encode("utf-8")),
        "selection": NATURAL_SCOPE,
        "first_word_offset_zero_based": 0,
        "normalized_sample_words": SPAN,
        "block_width": WIDTH,
        "top_frequency": count,
        "top_types": sorted(word for word, n in leading if n == count),
        "blocks": selected_blocks(words),
    }


def frequency_cap(natural):
    words = [word for block in natural["blocks"] for word in block]
    counts = Counter(words)
    first, second = counts.most_common(2)
    lead_word, max_count = first
    count_cap = second[1]
    if max_count == count_cap:
        return None
    order = sorted(
        (i for i, word in enumerate(words) if word == lead_word),
        key=lambda i: (digest(f"{METHOD_TAG}|{natural['id']}|{i}".encode("utf-8")), i),
    )
    cap_positions = sorted(order[:max_count - count_cap])
    for alias_number, i in enumerate(cap_positions, 1):
        alias = f"__p_j_044_clip_{alias_number}__"
        assert alias not in counts
        words[i] = alias
    capped = Counter(words)
    top_frequency = max(capped.values())
    top_types = sorted(word for word, n in capped.items() if n == top_frequency)
    assert top_frequency == count_cap and len(top_types) >= 2
    result = natural | {
        "id": f"{natural['id']}_frequency_capped",
        "parent_id": natural["id"],
        "selection": f"{NATURAL_SCOPE} Artificial token substitutions cap a unique highest-frequency type at the original second-highest count.",
        "selected_token_stream_sha256": digest(("\n".join(words) + "\n").encode("utf-8")),
        "source_selected_token_stream_sha256": natural["selected_token_stream_sha256"],
        "derivative": True,
        "deterministic_order_tag": METHOD_TAG,
        "replaced_word": lead_word,
        "replacement_positions_zero_based": cap_positions,
        "top_frequency": top_frequency,
        "top_types": top_types,
        "blocks": selected_blocks(words),
    }
    return result


def main():
    archive, out = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
    works = json.loads((archive / "external-streams.json").read_text())["works"]
    natural = [source_manifest(archive, work_id, record) for work_id, record in sorted(works.items())]
    assert len(natural) == len({entry["author"] for entry in natural}) == 6
    derived = [sample for entry in natural if (sample := frequency_cap(entry)) is not None]
    (out / "historical.json").write_text(json.dumps(natural, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
    (out / "historical-frequency-capped.json").write_text(json.dumps(derived, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
    for sample in natural + derived:
        print(sample["id"], len(sample["blocks"]), len(sample["blocks"][0]),
              sample["top_frequency"], len(sample["top_types"]),
              len(sample.get("replacement_positions_zero_based", [])), sample["selected_token_stream_sha256"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

prepare-external-streams.py.text:
"""Materialize capped historical word streams from verified body extracts."""

from argparse import ArgumentParser
from hashlib import sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re

from vs.refcorpus import normalize


CAP = 10000
PAIRS = (
    ("latin", "latin_bede", "latin_kempis"),
    ("english", "english_gower", "english_chaucer"),
    ("spanish", "spanish_lucanor", "spanish_buenamor"),
)


def digest(data):
    return sha256(data).hexdigest()


def checked(path, expected):
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if digest(data) != expected:
        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected digest: {path}")
    return data


def extended_ruiz(raw):
    start = re.search(r"^892 Dueñas,", raw, re.M).start()
    tail = raw[start:]
    end = re.search(r"^1230 Medio caño", tail, re.M).start()
    source = re.sub(r"\{\d+\}|\[[A-Z]\]", "", tail[:end])
    stanzas = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r"^\s*([0-9]+)\s+\S", source, re.M)]
    if stanzas != list(range(892, 1230)):
        raise ValueError("Unexpected Juan Ruiz stanza sequence")
    lines = [line for line in source.splitlines() if not line.strip().isupper()]
    if any(re.match(r"\s*\[\d+\]", line) for line in lines):
        raise ValueError("Unexpected editorial note in Juan Ruiz")
    return normalize("\n".join(lines), "spanish")


def prepare(archive, output):
    source_manifest = archive / "controls/manifest.json"
    entries = json.loads(source_manifest.read_text())["works"]
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths = output / "external-text"
    paths.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    works = {}
    for _, fit, evaluate in PAIRS:
        for name in (fit, evaluate):
            entry = entries[name]
            raw = checked(archive / entry["raw_file"], entry["raw_sha256"])
            base = checked(archive / entry["file"], entry["sha256"])
            full = base.decode("ascii")
            extraction = entry["body_boundary"]
            title = entry["title"]
            if name == "spanish_buenamor":
                full = extended_ruiz(raw.decode("utf-8-sig"))
                if not full.startswith(base.decode("ascii")):
                    raise ValueError("Extended Juan Ruiz text differs in existing body span")
                title = "Libro de Buen Amor, stanzas 892–1229"
                extraction = (
                    "From 892 Dueñas to immediately before 1230 Medio caño. "
                    "Verify all 338 stanza numbers after removing page braces. "
                    "Remove bracketed capital-letter markers and standalone uppercase headings."
                )
            if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+(?: [a-z]+)*", full):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid normalized stream: {name}")
            words = full.split()
            selected = " ".join(words[:CAP]).encode("ascii")
            if len(words) < 8000:
                raise ValueError(f"Fewer than 8000 words: {name}")
            rel = f"external-text/{name}.txt"
            (output / rel).write_bytes(selected)
            editorial = entry["source_notes"]
            works[name] = {
                "author": entry["author"],
                "title": title,
                "language": entry["language"],
                "date": entry["date"],
                "genre": entry["genre"],
                "edition": entry["edition"],
                "source_url": entry["url"],
                "catalog_url": entry.get("catalog_url"),
                "source_notes": editorial,
                "raw_archived_path": entry["raw_file"],
                "raw_sha256": entry["raw_sha256"],
                "previous_body_sha256": entry["sha256"],
                "body_extraction": extraction,
                "full_normalized_body_sha256": digest(full.encode("ascii")),
                "full_normalized_body_words": len(words),
                "selection": f"First {min(CAP, len(words))} normalized word tokens, in source order.",
                "file": rel,
                "sha256": digest(selected),
                "words": min(CAP, len(words)),
            }
    pair_entries = [
        {"id": lang, "fit": fit, "evaluation": evaluate} for lang, fit, evaluate in PAIRS
    ]
    manifest = {
        "works": works,
        "pairs": pair_entries,
        "word_stream": "ASCII lowercase alphabetic tokens separated by single spaces; no terminal newline.",
        "boundary_note": "Word order is retained; original line, sentence and page breaks are not represented.",
        "design": "One independently authored fit/evaluation work pair per language; no reciprocal duplication.",
        "prior_body_manifest_sha256": digest(source_manifest.read_bytes()),
        "prior_body_cleaner_sha256": digest((archive / "prepare-controls.py").read_bytes()),
    }
    (output / "external-streams.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
    )
    for key, info in works.items():
        print(key, info["words"], info["full_normalized_body_words"], info["sha256"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("padding_workdir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    prepare(args.padding_workdir, args.output)
